title: Sebastian and the Tryouts
premise: Ada Dravenmoor, the hockey team's statistician, has discovered that Coach Verlinden is fixing tryouts and games to keep a star player eligible — a player whose scholarship keeps the school's crumbling athletic program alive. When her statistics teacher pairs her with her nemesis, team captain Sebastian Kell, for a semester-long data audit project, the two are forced to examine the very numbers that prove the fraud. As their reluctant alliance deepens into trust and something more, they must decide whether exposing the rigging — and destroying the team, Sebastian's future, and the coach who once saved Ada from a worse life — is worth the truth. In the end, Ada testifies with Sebastian beside her, the championship is forfeited, and both learn that belonging bought with lies was never belonging at all.
about_author: Ada Nystrom grew up in a small mill town in northern Minnesota where high school hockey was the only religion, an obsession that left her equal parts devoted and skeptical. She writes young adult fiction about the kids who keep score from the sidelines.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Counts
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Opening day of hockey season: Ada records tryout data from the glass, invisible and precise. She notices an impossible stat — benched player Denny Ruiz's ice time defies every pattern. Emotional beat: isolation sharpened into vigilance; Ada counts days to graduation like a sentence.

chapters.title: Nemesis, Assigned
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ms. Okafor pairs Ada with Sebastian Kell for the semester statistics audit. Their history — a ruined group project, a public humiliation — makes the pairing a punishment. Sebastian smirks; Ada plots escape. Beat: dread, and a spark of reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: Cold Open
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian resents being paired with the girl who once called his playing 'statistically irrelevant.' But Coach Verlinden privately warns him to keep Ada away from team data. Beat: unease beneath bravado; Sebastian realizes the coach is afraid of her.

chapters.title: Outliers
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Forced together in the library, Ada and Sebastian clash over methodology — until the audit data surfaces the same anomaly Ada saw: Denny Ruiz's numbers don't exist. Someone fabricated his stats. Beat: grudging respect ignites into shared alarm.

chapters.title: The Coach's Favorite
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian confronts Verlinden gently; the coach deflects with a story about Denny's dying mother and the scholarship that keeps the program funded. Sebastian, who owes Verlinden everything, chooses loyalty — for now. Beat: guilt and divided allegiance.

chapters.title: Detention Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada digs into Denny's file and finds a forged transcript — and a note in Verlinden's handwriting. Sebastian catches her snooping and, instead of reporting her, covers for her. Beat: the enemy becomes a co-conspirator; trust begins, terrifyingly.

chapters.title: Home Ice
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A late-night practice; Sebastian shows Ada the rink after hours, teaching her to skate. Vulnerability cracks open: his scholarship depends on the team's survival, and exposure means losing everything. Beat: intimacy on thin ice, literally and otherwise.

chapters.title: What the Numbers Say
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The audit proves systematic fraud across three seasons. Ada wants to go to the principal; Sebastian begs for time — the championship is in two months, and scouts are coming. Beat: first real fracture between them; Ada feels her old invisibility returning.

chapters.title: The Whistle
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A rival school's athletic director hints he knows about Denny. Verlinden orders Sebastian to 'handle the statistician.' Sebastian refuses — and realizes the coach now sees him as a threat too. Beat: loyalty curdles into fear.

chapters.title: Ada, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada's locker is ransacked; her audit printouts gone. A warning follows: her financial aid 'could be reviewed.' Ada, a foster kid one mistake from losing her placement, understands the price of survival. Beat: terror, and the temptation to quit.

chapters.title: The Middle of It
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian finds Ada ready to burn the project and disappear. He gives her his backup copy of the data — he's been protecting it for weeks. Beat: the confession that changes everything; they are fully in it together now.

chapters.title: Denny Ruiz, Actual Person
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. They finally talk to Denny, who admits he never asked for any of it — Verlinden built him into a fraud to save the program, and Denny's mother believes her son is a star. Beat: the enemy gains a face; the moral stakes turn unbearable.

chapters.title: Intermission
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A rare quiet chapter: a school dance, a near-kiss, an agreement to decide together after the championship. Beat: stolen happiness, deliberately fragile — the reader knows the clock is running.

chapters.title: Game Fix
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. During a semifinal, Ada watches Verlinden pull Denny in a pattern that mirrors the doctored data exactly. She records everything. Verlinden sees her recording. Beat: open war declared with a single look across the ice.

chapters.title: Suspended Sentence
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Verlinden suspends Sebastian from the team for 'conduct violations' — retaliation dressed as discipline. The team turns on Sebastian; his scholarship hangs by a thread. Beat: the price of survival comes due, and Sebastian pays it standing.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Verlinden offers Ada a deal: destroy the audit and he'll fund her college, secure her placement, make her future safe. He's kind about it, which is worse. Beat: the devil's bargain, and Ada alone with the choice.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada almost signs. Then Denny's mother thanks her publicly for 'helping Denny's numbers shine' — and Ada realizes she'd be forging a person, the way she was once forged out of the record. Beat: the theme lands — belonging bought with lies isn't belonging.

chapters.title: Championship Eve
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The team wins its way to the final without Sebastian. Ada and Sebastian finish the audit overnight, building an airtight case — and a choice: expose Verlinden before the championship, or after. Beat: resolve forged in exhaustion and love.

chapters.title: The Game That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Championship day. Ada walks into the principal's office mid-game with the audit, Denny's statement, and Sebastian's testimony. The truth detonates: the title is forfeited, Verlinden suspended pending investigation. Beat: climax — victory that feels like ruin.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The aftermath is brutal: teammates who hate them, a scholarship in limbo, Denny's mother devastated. Sebastian loses the scouts, maybe the season, maybe more. Beat: grief and consequence — the price of survival, paid in full.

chapters.title: The One That Does
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Weeks later: Verlinden resigns; Denny, freed from the fraud, plays honestly and well; a scout who respects integrity offers Sebastian a walk-on chance. Ada's aid is restored — because she testified, not because she stayed silent. Beat: the championship that mattered was never on ice.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ada walks at graduation, no longer counting days but living one. Sebastian waits with two tickets to a real tryout — hers, as team analyst. Beat: resolution — belonging earned, identity chosen, the sentence served and the sentence rewritten.
